Accept additional cookies Reject additional cookies View cookies Hide cookie message Skip to main content Press release 100 new UK jobs created as Kuwait buys British-made AI-enabled air defence systems British jobs and skills will be boosted by a £370 million deal as Kuwait buys vital air defence systems from a UK-based business. From: Ministry of Defence and Luke Pollard MP Published: 9 October 2026 £370 million deal to strengthen Kuwait’s defences will create 100 UK jobs. British-built air defence systems to protect the Gulf state. Deal delivers on UK promise to back Gulf allies against regional threats. The contract with MARSS Systems Limited, an EOS company, will create 100 new jobs in the UK, supporting skilled engineering and manufacturing roles. MARSS will provide and integrate an advanced air defence system for Kuwait, incorporating jammers, radars and interceptors with its NiDAR platform, an AI-enabled command and control centre, to enhance the country’s ability to detect, deter and defeat airborne threats. The deal is set to expand MARSS’s offices in the UK, with production based in Bristol, demonstrating how defence investment can deliver good growth in every postcode by creating jobs and opportunity across the UK. The deal forms part of the UK’s Taskforce Sabre, which brings together government and industry to help Gulf states rapidly secure the systems and weapons they need. This follows Iran’s aggressive missile and drone attacks in the region. Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry, Luke Pollard MP, said: This deal is a clear demonstration of the UK delivering on its promise to support our regional partners. By backing Kuwait with world-leading British technology, we’re not just strengthening a vital ally’s defences against real and growing threats. We’re creating skilled jobs here at home and proving that UK industry can deliver when it matters most. CEO of MARSS, Johannes Pinl, said: Countering drones and aerial threats is not about any single system, it is about an intelligent, layered architecture that detects, decides and defeats within seconds, and MARSS has built exactly that. Through 2027, MARSS will integrate the sensors and effectors that protect Kuwait’s people, critical infrastructure and national assets, backed by British engineering and new skilled jobs here in the UK. The UK has already supported Kuwait with Rapid Sentry, a ground-based air defence missile system. The RAF’s ORCUS system is also operating in the country, helping personnel detect drones early and take decisive action. This latest deal builds on existing support, cementing the UK’s role as a trusted defence partner to Kuwait and the wider Gulf region. article.body:
UK MoD reports £370m Kuwait air-defence contract; integration remains ahead

The UK Ministry of Defence has announced a £370 million contract for MARSS Systems Limited to provide and integrate an air-defence system for Kuwait. It combines jammers, radars and interceptors with the company’s NiDAR AI-enabled command and control centre to address airborne threats. MARSS says integration will run through 2027, and the contract is expected to create 100 UK jobs. The contract exists; the announcement does not establish that the new system is integrated or operational in Kuwait.
